Prevention: Remove the infected and exposed trees.
Control leaf miners on young trees and certain cultivars as galleries can create secondary infections.
Plant trees that are less susceptible or more tolerant.
Install/plant windbreaks to reduce the spread and severity of the disease.
Monitoring: Asian leaf miner ( Phyllocnistis citrella ) can infest leaves, stems, and fruit.
Numerous cracks occur in the cuticle covering leaf miner galleries, providing means for bacteria to penetrate directly into the palisade.
Citrus canker lesions start as pinpoint spots and attain a maximum size of 2 to 10 mm in diameter.
Lesions become visible about 7 to 10 days after infection on the underside of leaves and soon thereafter on the upper surface.
The most critical period for fruit rind infection is during the first 90 days after petal fall.
Fruit can also act as an indicator of time of infection.
Lesion age can be estimated on fruit and help determine when infection occurred.
Regularly check your orchard and report any unusual or unfamiliar symptoms.
Direct Control: Leaves, stems, and fruit become resistant to infection as they mature unless they are wounded.
Restrictions: Disinfect agricultural implements, hands and clothes while treating the citrus.
July on oranges and three to four applications of copper-containing fungicides during this period, at 3-week intervals, should be sufficient to obtain relatively clean fruit.
